To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in patients without primary liver disease and with abnormal hepatic tests, a 10% weight reduction will improve the hepatic tests and physical findings related with the liver.
weight reduction of greater or equal than 10% in overweight adults with abnormal liver function tests, without primary liver disease improves liver function tests and resolves hepatosplenomegalia.
weight reduction of greater or equal to 5% corrected abnormal hepetic test results in overweight adults and decreased hepatosplenomgaly in those with primary liver disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of weight loss on hepatic test result and physical findings related with the liver.
the effect of weight loss on the liver.
the effect of weight loss on liver function in obese patients with or without liver disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in overweight adults, weight reduction is a reasonable and cost-effective initial step in the evaluation of an isolated abnormality in hepatic tests.
weight loss in the overweight patient is associated with improvement in hepatic test results.
the effect of weight loss in the treatment of fatty liver in obese patients is not well established.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of weight loss in overweight adults with abnormal hepatic tests is not well defined.
the weight loss in obese individuals is associated with a significant reduction of liver enzymes.

weight loss can improve abnormal liver test results in overweight individuals without primary liver disease and that the magnitude of weight loss is directly related to the magnitude of improvement in liver test results.
The main takeaway from our work is that
if you have a patient who is obese and has abnormal liver tests, you should consider trying weight loss.
weight loss is an important therapeutic intervention for the treatment of NAFLD, especially when it is combined with other interventions, such as physical activity, diet modification, and medication.

in the absence of other causes of abnormal hepatic test findings and physical signs, weight reduction is effective in correcting abnormal liver function and improving physical signs of hepatomegaly and splenomegaly in overweight patients.
